Boy dies, 4 family members critical after fire rips through Bronx apartment: report

A boy has died and four members of his family are critical after a fire ripped through a Bronx apartment early Wednesday, according to a report.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

A boy has died and four members of his family are critical after a lithium battery sparked a fire that ripped through a Bronx apartment building early Wednesday, according to officials.

Some 130 fire and EMS personnel raced to the Patterson Houses complex on Morris Ave just after 12:50 a.m. to fight the deadly blaze in an apartment on the 11th floor of the 13-story building

The all-hands fire was caused by a “lithium-ion battery,” the FDNY later confirmed, with neighbors telling The Post the family used an e-bike that was charged in their kitchen.

Two adults and three boys, all thought to be from the same family, were rescued, with a 15-year-old boy, a 37-year-old man, a 33-year-old woman and a so-far unidentified male all hospitalized in critical condition.

A fifth person could not be saved, the FDNY said, with sources telling WABC he was a boy who was between the age of 12 to 16.

Neighbors described him as a “young, vibrant and very energetic” boy who “loved basketball.”

All of the victims suffered burn injuries and inhaled smoke.

A makeshift memorial of candles and a plush bear have been left at the scene.
